title: Cache instrumentation overhead results (prefix/KV cache telemetry v2)
content:
Doc purpose
- Summarize perf overhead from KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 instrumentation (lookup/insert/evict hooks + per-request outcome classification + saved_prefill_ms estimation).
- Data used to validate ENG-4813/4814 acceptance criterion: <1% overhead at p95 on representative workloads.
- NOTE: These results are from synthetic cache-heavy benchmarks and should be treated as “upper bound” for production (prod has more network/gateway time).

Builds / toggles
- Baseline build: runtime main @ 2025-02-05 (pre-instrumentation)
- Instrumented build: runtime main @ 2025-02-21 (includes PR-18421 + PR-18436 + PR-18452)
- Instrumentation flags:
  - runtime.cache_telemetry_v2.enabled = true|false
  - runtime.cache_telemetry_v2.sampling_rate = 1.0 (unless noted)
  - runtime.cache_telemetry_v2.export_mode = counters (default) vs event_payload (structured outcome event)
- Metrics sink used for benchmark: in-process no-op sink for counters; JSON serialization enabled only in “event_payload” runs.

Hardware + software
- GPU SKUs tested
  - NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe)
  - NVIDIA H100 80GB (SXM)
  - NVIDIA L40S 48GB
- CPU: dual-socket x86_64 (baseline in fleet), 512GB RAM
- Runtime config (common)
  - continuous batching enabled
  - KV cache enabled (prefix cache enabled for cacheable scenarios)
  - tensor parallel: 1 (single GPU) for comparability across SKUs
  - model: Redwood-verified 7B class (decoder-only) for microbench; see notes for long-context pass

Workloads / scenarios
We ran three request-mix scenarios to cover the common sequence length distributions we see in Hosted + Dedicated:
- S1: “Short chat”
  - prompt_tokens: p50 180 / p95 380
  - gen_tokens: p50 120 / p95 240
  - cacheability: high (80% of traffic shares one of 20 prefixes)
- S2: “Mixed SaaS”
  - prompt_tokens: p50 450 / p95 1400
  - gen_tokens: p50 180 / p95 420
  - cacheability: medium (50% shared prefixes; long tail)
- S3: “Long context / RAG-ish”
  - prompt_tokens: p50 2.4k / p95 6.5k
  - gen_tokens: p50 220 / p95 480
  - cacheability: low to medium (20–35% shared prefixes)

Measurements captured
- End-to-end latency (request start -> last token) p50/p95
- Prefill latency p50/p95 (model forward for prompt)
- Decode token rate (tokens/sec) p50 (batch steady-state)
- CPU overhead: runtime process CPU% delta (averaged over steady 5 min)
- Allocation rate delta (bytes/sec) from jemalloc stats (spot-check)


============================
Table A — A100 80GB results (sampling_rate=1.0, counters export)
============================
Columns:

- tok_s_delta_%:   -0.65%
- CPU delta: +0.6% absolute (e.g., 38.1% -> 38.7%)

S2 (Mixed SaaS)
- Baseline_p95_ms: 1048

- p95_overhead_%:  +0.76%
- Baseline_prefill_p95_ms: 312

- Baseline_tok_s:  1415

S3 (Long context / RAG-ish)

- p95_overhead_%:  +0.73%
- Baseline_prefill_p95_ms: 1884

Notes (A100)
- The dominant overhead is in CPU-side accounting and atomic increments, not GPU kernels.
- Allocation rate delta was within noise for counters-only (<= +0.5% bytes/sec). No measurable allocator regression.

Notes (H100)
- Similar % overhead as A100; absolute ms deltas smaller in S1/S2 due to faster baseline.
- No visible change in GPU utilization; CPU remains the limiter for telemetry paths.

- p95_overhead_%:  +1.07%

Notes (L40S)
- Slightly above the <1% p95 target in these synthetic runs, but still close. This SKU is more sensitive because baseline is slower and CPU time becomes a larger fraction of E2E.
- Recommendation: default sampling_rate=0.5 for L40S tiers if we see real-world regressions; validate in Hosted us-west L40S pool during staged rollout.


============================
Table D — Structured event payload export (worst-case)
============================
Purpose: quantify overhead when runtime exports per-request structured payload (used for outcome classification debugging / initial data validation). This is NOT expected to be the steady-state for all traffic.
Config deltas vs above:
- runtime.cache_telemetry_v2.export_mode = event_payload
- JSON serialization enabled
- sampling_rate = 1.0

A100, S2 (Mixed SaaS)
- Baseline_p95_ms: 1048
- Counters_p95_ms: 1056  (+0.76%)
- Event_p95_ms:    1084  (+3.44%)
- CPU delta vs baseline: +3.1% absolute

H100, S2 (Mixed SaaS)
- Baseline_p95_ms: 778
- Counters_p95_ms: 782   (+0.51%)
- Event_p95_ms:    800   (+2.83%)
- CPU delta vs baseline: +2.6% absolute

Interpretation
- As expected, per-request payload + JSON dominates overhead.
- Action: keep event_payload behind a separate short-lived validation flag; default to counters for broad enablement.


============================
Table E — Sampling rate sensitivity (counters export)
============================
Scenario: A100, S1 and S3

A100, S1 (Short chat)
- sampling_rate=1.0: p95_overhead +0.97%
- sampling_rate=0.5: p95_overhead +0.62%
- sampling_rate=0.1: p95_overhead +0.18%

A100, S3 (Long context)
- sampling_rate=1.0: p95_overhead +0.73%
- sampling_rate=0.5: p95_overhead +0.49%
- sampling_rate=0.1: p95_overhead +0.12%

Notes
- Overhead roughly scales with sampling rate for the CPU-side increments/logging.
- Sampling interacts with accuracy; telemetry spec should pin minimum effective sample size per route/model bucket (Logan/Thomas to confirm).


Key takeaways (summary)
1) Counters-only export meets <1% p95 overhead on A100 and H100 across the three scenarios tested.
2) L40S is slightly over 1% in this synthetic harness (~1.05–1.09% p95). This is close enough that we should validate in a small real-world canary before broad rollout.
3) Structured event payload export (JSON) is 2.8–3.4% p95 overhead and should be treated as debugging/short-term validation only.
4) saved_prefill_ms estimation (PR-18436) did not create an observable additional regression beyond the base hook/counter costs; overhead appears dominated by accounting + sink calls.

Open questions / TODOs
- [ ] Confirm L40S production canary with real gateway/network overhead included (Connor + Omar). Target: verify E2E p95 overhead <1% when measured from client perspective.
- [ ] Validate “partial-prefill” heavy scenario (streaming retries / interrupted requests) because it increases cache event frequency; likely to stress classification counters (Samir).
- [ ] Decide whether we need a separate cheaper codepath for saved_prefill_ms under very high QPS (Omar/Noah).
- [ ] Align with telemetry pipeline expectations: if sampling_rate < 1.0, ensure dashboards compute hit-rate unbiasedly (Logan/Nadia/Mei).

Changelog
- 2025-02-06: initial sheet created, baseline numbers from A100 only
- 2025-02-18: added H100 + L40S sweeps
- 2025-02-22: added structured event payload section and sampling sensitivity
- 2025-02-24: updated to include PR-18452 outcome classification build; minor reruns for S2 variance
